Subject: POC trial environment setup  FinLytics / Redwood

Thanks again for a productive call earlier, Emma and Jacob  great context on your high-throughput search and summarization use cases. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the proposed POC plan and the options for trial environment so we can lock timelines and owners.

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 200ms for typical seq lengths (~512 tokens)
- Throughput: sustain 50 requests/sec with concurrent users (burst to 150)
- Embedding quality: 95% of similarity search results match baseline benchmarks you provided
- Cost: target < $X per 1M tokens (we'll provide estimates once you pick model variant)
- Data controls: 30-day retention, audit logs, SOC2 evidence available

Evaluation plan / timeline (recommended):
- Week 0 (by 2026-06-16): Provision trial environment and provide onboarding docs
- Week 1 (2026-06-17 to 2026-06-23): Baseline tests (latency/throughput/embeddings) and quick functional workshop
- Week 2 (2026-06-24 to 2026-06-30): App-driven load tests + quality evals against your prompt set
- Week 3-4: Iteration and handoff; decision point at end of week 4

Environment options (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API trial (fastest)  Redwood-managed, no infra on your side; great for quick results and monitoring. Recommended default for a 4-week POC.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool)  predictable throughput, better isolation; ~3-5 business days to provision.
3) VPC trial / Private deployment  full network control and data plane in your VPC; longer lead time (2-4 weeks) and additional compliance review.

Our recommendation: start with a hosted API trial so you can get baseline metrics quickly, then move to a Dedicated sandbox if you need strict isolation or to a VPC trial for long-term deployment.

Next steps / asks for FinLytics:
1) Confirm preferred environment (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC).
2) Confirm model preference (we can suggest variants optimized for latency/cost if you'd like).
3) Share any required security/compliance docs and a contact for network/security questions.

I've attached a short SOC2 summary and the proposed POC-MAP workbook to help scope tests. If you approve hosted, we can provision a trial account-sized sandbox by 2026-06-16 and schedule the onboarding workshop for 06-17.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Summary.pdf, POC-MAP-20260612.xlsx

Thanks Marissa  this is helpful. Quick answers from our side: we are comfortable starting with a hosted trial as long as we get SOC2 evidence, data retention controls, and network egress constraints documented. We want to avoid full VPC work unless absolutely necessary during the POC.

Our success criteria (finalized):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms (as you suggested)
- Throughput: steady 50 req/s during peak tests; support spikes to 150 req/s
- Embedding accuracy: top-5 retrieval precision >= 0.95 on our sample set
- Data retention: 30 days with audit log access

Start date: we can aim to start the hosted trial week of 2026-06-17. Please provide a short network requirements spreadsheet (firewall rules, IP ranges, egress ports) and a sample SLA / uptime target. Also include any guidance on token limits and rate-limiting so we can coordinate load testing.

Attaching our initial network worksheet (network_requirements.xlsx).

Cheers,

FinLytics

Got it  I can provision a hosted trial sandbox for FinLytics. Questions / notes:

- Default rate limits: we provision at 100 req/s by default for trials (burst up to 200)  if Emma needs steady 50 req/s we're good, but will set rate-limits explicitly on the account.
- Model variants: recommend starting with a latency-optimized variant (gpt-redwood-latency-v1) for generation tests and a higher-accuracy variant for embedding comparisons. If FinLytics prefers a named model, we can pin it.
- Pre-warm: we can pre-warm the KV cache and run a short warmup suite to stabilize p95 numbers before the workshop.

I'll wait for the network spreadsheet and the contact list to finish provisioning.
